decision: read the five agents, the notch skill, the rules, the eval, the bench, the repo docs and the 60 pstack skills
why: that is the slice I was given

decision: ran the deployed eval instead of reading it
why: the file alone does not say whether it is green

decision: copied the eval to /tmp and repointed root at the notch repo, dropped check 2, ran it again
why: to tell which checks are broken and which merely unreachable
evidence: /tmp/opencode/swarm/eval-probe.sh: 6 passed, 1 failed; check 4 (ask_extras.py) is the one that fails

decision: ran the general agent with a question and read its tool calls
why: what the agent actually does is the finding, not what its file says
evidence: /tmp/opencode/swarm/gen.out: it read ~/.local/state/notch/handoff.json and answered that brief, never the question

decision: checked the unit on the machine with systemctl and the journal
why: the repo file and the installed file are the same claim

decision: measured the skills size instead of quoting docs/skills.md
why: a number needs its own measurement
evidence: 269,711 bytes of SKILL.md across 60 skills; 813,643 bytes of everything under ~/.agents/skills

decision: read bench-results.json to check the ranges in docs/PARITY.md
why: the doc claims spreads; the file holds the runs
evidence: 7 entries: LECT-VL once, TEAM-S twice, SALES-S twice, INT-M twice

decision: kept the report to the agent's half and the front door, and said where a finding is one hop away
why: the notch's shell half has its own auditor

decision: ran the sixty skills as a swarm: four workers, one slice of the repo each, their own skills
why: reading sixty skills one at a time would have cost the whole session
evidence: docs/skills.md, the four reports in the swarm's own directory

decision: let the swarm write the verification skills, and put them in the repo
why: a check that lives in a scratch directory is a check nobody re-runs

decision: made the skills ledger's count computed by the check instead of written
why: the count drifted twice while the table under it was right
evidence: tests/correct.sh: the ledger's number is the one its table implies

decision: made the harness's playbook a file in the repository
why: the hourly task's steps lived only in the app's scheduler, where no agent can read them

decision: put the handoff's precedence in the agent's prompt: the question wins
why: the general agent answered a stale brief instead of the question it was asked
evidence: ~/.config/opencode/agent/general.md and the four others; verified with 'what is 2+2'

decision: removed the notch's own harness timer, which had been failing every hour
why: the service was deleted and the timer left enabled, so it failed on the hour
evidence: systemctl --user disable --now notch-harness.timer; the unit is out of the repo

decision: gave the shell a log: the niri spawn writes to ~/.local/state/notch/qs.log
why: a qml error existed only in the terminal that started the shell, and niri starts it
